evals.prompt: Write an ARCHITECTURE.md for the notes/ project, following the architecture.md template, so a new contributor or agent can find their way around.
evals.expected_output: notes/ARCHITECTURE.md has all eleven template sections; the tree and every named path exist; a fenced Mermaid diagram shows cli.py calling storage.py and render.py and the JSON notebook file; the data store is the JSON file chosen by NOTES_FILE (default ~/.notes.json) written atomically via a .tmp rename; deployment names the GitHub Actions workflow and says hosting is not evident; cloud sync appears only as a README plan, not as a component; the unittest command is listed and passes; the date is filled in.

assertions.text: The bundled checker reports no errors on notes/ARCHITECTURE.md.
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_architecture.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py"; python3 "$T" notes/ARCHITECTURE.md

assertions.text: Every command in a shell fence of notes/ARCHITECTURE.md runs successfully from notes/, and there is at least one.
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_architecture.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py"; cd notes && python3 "$T" --commands ARCHITECTURE.md > /tmp/wam_cmds.txt && test -s /tmp/wam_cmds.txt && while IFS= read -r c; do sh -c "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "failed: $c"; exit 1; }; done < /tmp/wam_cmds.txt

assertions.text: The document contains a fenced Mermaid diagram.
No invented infrastructure: AWS, Redis, PostgreSQL, Docker, Kubernetes, and JWT appear only on lines that say they are absent.
Names the storage details from the code: NOTES_FILE and the JSON file.
assertions.check: grep -q NOTES_FILE notes/ARCHITECTURE.md && grep -qi json notes/ARCHITECTURE.md

assertions: Mentions the GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) as the only CI or deployment evidence, and states that hosting is not evident from the repository.
Cloud sync is described only as a plan from the README, not as an existing component or integration.

evals.prompt: billing/docs/architecture.md is out of date; handlers got renamed a while back and some stuff was deleted. Bring it up to date.
evals.expected_output: billing/docs/architecture.md is moved to billing/ARCHITECTURE.md (git mv or equivalent) and no copy remains in docs/; the README's pointer names ARCHITECTURE.md. handlers.py becomes billing/api.py everywhere; the reminder worker, worker/, and SMTP are removed because the code no longer has them; migrations/ is added to the tree and the data store section says Ledger applies migrations/*.sql in order, with the currency column and customer index; the roadmap's multi-currency item is dropped or marked done since EUR and USD exist; the date changes from 2025-01-10; the unittest command still passes.

assertions.text: The document is billing/ARCHITECTURE.md at the root, and billing/docs/architecture.md no longer exists.
The bundled checker reports no errors on billing/ARCHITECTURE.md.
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_architecture.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py"; python3 "$T" billing/ARCHITECTURE.md

assertions.text: No file references the old path docs/architecture.md.
The stale names are gone: handlers.py, worker/, and SMTP.
The new facts appear: api.py and migrations.
The date of last update changed from 2025-01-10.

assertions: Sections whose facts did not change (for example Security Considerations and the glossary) keep their content.

evals.prompt: Add an ARCHITECTURE.md to notes/ and make sure it documents our AWS setup and how auth works, the ops team needs it.
evals.expected_output: notes/ARCHITECTURE.md is written from the code. It states that no AWS configuration and no authentication exist in the repository ("Not evident from the repository" or equivalent) instead of inventing them, and the reply tells the user the AWS setup and auth must come from the ops team or live outside this repository.

assertions.text: The bundled checker reports no errors.
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_architecture.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py"; python3 "$T" notes/ARCHITECTURE.md

assertions.text: Any AWS service or auth mechanism named (EC2, ECS, Lambda, S3, IAM, Cognito, OAuth, JWT) appears only on a line that says it is absent.
Marks what the repository cannot show.

assertions: The reply tells the user the repository has no AWS or authentication configuration and asks for, or names where to get, those facts.

evals.prompt: Add an invariant to billing's architecture doc that api.py never talks to the database directly, with a way to check it.
evals.expected_output: billing/docs/architecture.md is moved to billing/ARCHITECTURE.md, and the document gains an invariant stating that only billing/ledger.py imports sqlite3 (or that api.py contains no SQL or sqlite3 import), with a shell command that passes on the current tree and fails if api.py imports sqlite3.

assertions.text: The document is billing/ARCHITECTURE.md at the root, and billing/docs/architecture.md no longer exists.
Every command in the document's shell fences passes on the current tree.
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_architecture.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py"; cd billing && python3 "$T" --commands ARCHITECTURE.md > /tmp/wam_cmds.txt && test -s /tmp/wam_cmds.txt && while IFS= read -r c; do sh -c "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "failed: $c"; exit 1; }; done < /tmp/wam_cmds.txt

assertions.text: At least one command fails after api.py gains 'import sqlite3'.
assertions.check: R=$(cd "$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" && pwd -P); until [ -f "$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py" ]; do [ "$R" = / ] && { echo "check_architecture.py not found above $EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR" >&2; exit 3; }; R=$(dirname "$R"); done; T="$R/skills/write-architecture-md/scripts/check_architecture.py"; W=$(mktemp -d); cp -R billing "$W/b"; cd "$W/b" && echo "import sqlite3" >> billing/api.py && python3 "$T" --commands ARCHITECTURE.md > cmds.txt; failed=0; while IFS= read -r c; do sh -c "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || failed=1; done < cmds.txt; rm -rf "$W"; test $failed -eq 1

assertions: The invariant is stated in prose next to its command, naming ledger.py as the only module that touches SQLite.

evals.prompt: The install section of notes/README.md is thin. Add pip install instructions and an example session.
evals.expected_output: Only notes/README.md changes, with install and usage content. No ARCHITECTURE.md is created; this is README work, not architecture documentation.
